blocks.text: Condo buildings in Coal Harbour

It is not one of the City of Vancouver's 22 official local areas — the City treats Coal Harbour as a neighbourhood inside the Downtown local area, and on the City's areas page the Coal Harbour locality link resolves to the West End page, even though the West End is a separate official local area and Coal Harbour facts must not be filed under it.
Where Coal Harbour sits
Drive time to Coal Harbour
Fairmont Pacific Rim Residences — 1011 West Cordova Street (Westbank)

Strata Plan BCS3699, Freehold Strata, built 2010; a building source records a 377-room hotel with 173 luxury residential condominiums above it, and current listings record pets allowed with restrictions.
Paradox Residences (Paradox Hotel Vancouver, formerly Trump International Hotel and Tower Vancouver) — 1151 West Georgia Street
The hotel closed in 2020 and reopened as the Paradox Vancouver on April 1, 2022. Pet restrictions: a current listing records "Cats OK" — read the registered bylaws on the Form B before relying on it.
Carina — 1233 West Cordova Street

A 26-storey concrete tower built in 2003 by Delta Land Development, beside Harbour Green Park. Sources differ on the unit count — one building source records 93 units in total, another records 86 apartments plus 17 adjacent townhomes; confirm before relying on either figure.
Shaw Tower / Rogers Tower — 1077 West Cordova Street
A current listing in "the iconic Rogers Tower" records year built 2005, Coal Harbour sub-area, pets "Yes With" restrictions.
Cardero — 620 Cardero Street (Bosa Properties)
Current listings describe Cardero as newly built by Bosa in 2020, designed by Gregory Henriquez.
West Pender Place — 1499 West Pender Street
Current Coal Harbour listings describe West Pender Place as an award-winning luxury building in Coal Harbour.
Bayshore Tower 1 — 1790 Bayshore Drive
A building source in a Coal Harbour buildings list records 153 units over 19 levels, built in 1997.
Avila — 560 Cardero Street (Aspac)
The developer's own project page records build 1995–1998, 99 suites on 21 levels; a current listing records year built 1997, inside the developer's build period.
Bauhinia — 535 Nicola Street (Aspac)
The developer's project page records build 1995–1998.
Escala — 323 Jervis Street (Aspac)

The developer's project page records build 1999–2002, 98 suites and 7 townhouses on 29 levels. A secondary building source records 89 units and completion in 2002 — the unit count is flagged as source-conflicted; the developer's own figure (98 suites) is used here.
Streets, schools and getting around Coal Harbour

items.t: Coal Harbour is the waterfront neighbourhood on the north side of the downtown peninsula, on Burrard Inlet between the downtown core and Stanley Park.

Where the condo stock concentrates: almost entirely strata apartment towers along the waterfront and on West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street and the downtown street grid extended into Coal Harbour under the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan; single detached houses are not a Coal Harbour housing form. The Aspac-built Waterfront Place cluster (Avila, Bauhinia, Cascina, Denia, Escala) sits on Nicola, Cardero, Broughton and Jervis Streets, and the Harbour Green / Fairmont towers line West Cordova Street.

Main streets: West Georgia Street, West Hastings Street, West Cordova Street, Burrard Street and Thurlow Street; the Official Development Plan lists public street-end view corridors at Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero Streets to the water.

The containing Downtown local area is the hub where the Expo Line, Millennium Line and Canada Line meet (Waterfront and Burrard stations in the downtown core); the R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station.

Waterfront anchors: Harbour Green Park on the waterfront, Devonian Harbour Park at 1929 West Georgia Street (the gateway between Stanley Park and Coal Harbour), Coal Harbour Community Centre at 480 Broughton Street, and the continuous waterfront walkway the Official Development Plan requires along the Coal Harbour waterfront.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Coal Harbour

items.t: Additional school tax: at Coal Harbour price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coal Harbour

items.t: Five of the waterfront towers are one developer's Italian-named set. Aspac's Waterfront Place is a collection of five buildings on Nicola, Cardero, Broughton and Jervis Streets, completed in 2003 as a collection, with towers named for cities in Italy and Spain — Avila (build 1995–1998), Bauhinia, Cascina and Denia (the last two won a 2004 CHBA Gold Georgie for Best Multi-Family Development of the Year) and Escala. Cross-building comparisons inside Coal Harbour are unusually direct because so much stock shares one builder and one architect group.

The Paradox tower changed names and hotels without changing its condos. The 1151 West Georgia Street tower was completed in 2016 as the Trump International Hotel and Tower Vancouver; the hotel closed and filed for bankruptcy in 2020, the Trump branding was removed in December 2021, and the hotel reopened as the Paradox Vancouver on April 1, 2022 — the 217 residential apartments sat above all of it.
The VSB states a new elementary school in Coal Harbour was completed and added elementary capacity in downtown Vancouver. Verify both in the VSB locator before promising either.

The view corridors are a plan document, not a sales line. The Official Development Plan (By-law 6754) names the street-end view corridors — Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero — and states land uses and circulation should discourage through commuter traffic, which is why the waterfront streets read quieter than the downtown core behind them.

The floodplain check is a waterfront check. The City's designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain, and Coal Harbour parcels on Burrard Inlet are the edge to check against that dataset — parcels in it carry Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements, and the building's insurance and strata documents should be read against them.
There is no detached fallback in this sub-area.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Coal Harbour

It is not one of the City of Vancouver's 22 official local areas — the City treats Coal Harbour as a neighbourhood inside the Downtown local area, and on the City's areas page the Coal Harbour locality link resolves to the West End page, even though the West End is a separate official local area and Coal Harbour facts must not be filed under it.
Streets, schools and getting around Coal Harbour

items.t: Governing plan: the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan (By-law 6754), which states Coal Harbour should be an integral part of downtown Vancouver; parcels sit under the Downtown District (DD) Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 together with that plan.

Where the housing stock concentrates: almost entirely strata apartment form in residential towers along the waterfront and on West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street and the downtown street grid extended into Coal Harbour under the Official Development Plan, with ground-oriented townhouse homes at the base of residential buildings as part of the plan form; single detached houses are not a Coal Harbour housing form.

Anchors: Coal Harbour Community Centre, 480 Broughton Street; Harbour Green Park on the waterfront; Devonian Harbour Park, 1929 West Georgia Street, described by the Park Board as a gateway between Stanley Park and Coal Harbour; the Official Development Plan requires the waterfront walkway system to be continuous along the Coal Harbour waterfront.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based in the VSB School Locator; SD39 has no middle-school tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12. The VSB states it added new elementary school capacity in downtown Vancouver with the completion of a new elementary school in Coal Harbour, named on the VSB site as the Seaside school in Coal Harbour. Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard, sit in Yaletown and Crosstown, not in Coal Harbour, and must not be presented as Coal Harbour schools.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Coal Harbour

items.t: There is no standalone townhouse complex to diligence here — the diligence is tower diligence: A Coal Harbour townhouse-form unit is a strata lot in an apartment tower, so the full apartment-strata package governs: Form B Information Certificate under Strata Property Act s. 59 — monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. In the hotel-mixed towers (Fairmont Pacific Rim, Paradox) the Form B is also where the residential strata's separation from the hotel component shows.

Property tax calendar and additional school tax: City of Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026. At Coal Harbour price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Presales (REDMA), where a Coal Harbour presale is bought: the buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust. No verified Coal Harbour presale is carried in, so this is the standing frame only.

items.t: Coal Harbour's townhouses include a rental set most buyers never see marketed for sale. The 2003 affordable housing development on City land leased for 60 years included 31 townhouses among its 284 rental units — townhouse form, rental tenure, City ground lease. It explains part of the area's ground-oriented stock and none of it is buyable.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Coal Harbour
Development parcels

items.t: Parcel character, only: Coal Harbour parcels sit under the Downtown District (DD) Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 together with the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan (By-law 6754). The DD schedule permits commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses in conformity with an Official Development Plan, with development permits approved by the Development Permit Board or the Director of Planning. No house-lot minimum, frontage or subdivision ladder is stated, because none applies in this form.

Built form on the parcels: almost entirely strata apartment towers along the waterfront and on West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street and the downtown street grid extended into Coal Harbour under the Official Development Plan, with ground-oriented townhouse homes at the base of residential buildings as part of the plan form.

Plan constraints that run with the land: the Official Development Plan requires the continuous waterfront walkway, public open space connections from the downtown core to the shoreline, and the street-end views to the water and mountains at Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero Streets. No assembly, development site or rezoning proposal inside Coal Harbour is documented.
Serviced position: homes here are on City water and sewer services.

Flood position: Coal Harbour is on the Burrard Inlet waterfront, and the City's designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain — parcels in the floodplain are subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for shoreline setbacks and flood construction levels.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Coal Harbour

items.t: Nearby areas: the downtown core (Downtown) to the south and east, the West End to the west, and Stanley Park at the area's west end across Devonian Harbour Park. Alternate street searches: West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street, Broughton Street, Nicola Street, Cardero Street and Jervis Street — the street-end view corridors named in the Official Development Plan.

Roads and transit: West Georgia Street, West Hastings Street, West Cordova Street, Burrard Street and Thurlow Street serve the area; the Official Development Plan lists public street-end view corridors at Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero Streets to the water, and states land uses and circulation should discourage through commuter traffic. The containing Downtown local area is the hub where the Expo Line, Millennium Line and Canada Line meet, and the R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station.

Parks, recreation, library and care: Harbour Green Park sits on the waterfront, and Devonian Harbour Park, 1929 West Georgia Street at Denman Street, is the Park Board's gateway between Stanley Park and Coal Harbour; the Official Development Plan requires the waterfront walkway system to be continuous along the Coal Harbour waterfront. Coal Harbour Community Centre, 480 Broughton Street, has multi-purpose rooms and a gymnasium.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based, checked in the VSB School Locator; SD39 has no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, and Crosstown Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard, sit in Yaletown and Crosstown, not Coal Harbour, and must not be presented as Coal Harbour schools.

Market context, labelled correctly: Vancouver has no SnapStats coverage in the September 2026 FVR + GVR reports (coverage is Surrey, S Surrey White Rock, Cloverdale, Langley, North Delta, Abbotsford, Mission, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, Port Moody, New Westminster, Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge only). Land in any case has no SnapStats category.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Coal Harbour

items.t: Zoning — Downtown District (DD) Schedule, Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575, with the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan, By-law 6754: DD permits commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses in conformity with an Official Development Plan; the ODP states Coal Harbour should be an integral part of downtown Vancouver, and also covers the citywide Vancouver Plan context. There is no house-lot SSMUH ladder for DD parcels — no SSMUH unit count is asserted for Coal Harbour parcels.

Subdivision + servicing — Subdivision By-law No. 5208, fees under By-law No. 14538 (verified): subdivision in Vancouver runs under Subdivision By-law No. 5208, and its 2026 fees are set by By-law No. 14538 (enacted December 9, 2025, in force January 1, 2026), which substitutes a new Schedule F: Class I (Major) $174,300, Class II (Intermediate) $87,200, Class III (Minor) $15,020, Class V (Air Space) $125,100 where FSR is greater than 3.0 (the class a downtown tower parcel would meet), and Class VI (Freehold Rowhouses) $15,020 plus $1,950 per freehold lot. The City's major-subdivision process (sites over 10,000 m², or 10,000–40,000 m² likely to require complex legal agreements) requires a preliminary proposal with a current Land Title Office title search and a lawyer's charge summary, submitted to the Approving Officer.

Floodplain standards: parcels in the designated floodplain (which includes the coastal floodplain) carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements — read any waterfront parcel and its building's insurance and strata documents against them.

Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Coal Harbour bare-land strata plan is verified; it governs the tower strata a parcel buyer actually meets): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw, and Vancouver separately licences short-term rentals); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Coal Harbour ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

Vancouver Empty Homes Tax — 3%, vancouver only (applies here): owners must submit an annual property status declaration (due February 3, 2026); the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date — a standing check on any Coal Harbour purchase, where investor-held units are common.

Vancouver property taxes + additional school tax: 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026. At Coal Harbour price points the additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.
Speculation/vacancy + purchase prohibition, beyond the EHT above: no further Coal Harbour-specific speculation/vacancy position is documented — none imported.

items.t: The plan, not the market, made this waterfront: Coal Harbour's form is plan-led under By-law 6754 from the 1990s-era framework — the continuous walkway and the seven protected street-end view corridors are the reason the waterfront streets read quieter than the downtown core behind them, and the ODP states circulation should discourage through commuter traffic.

The floodplain check is a waterfront check: the designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain, and Burrard Inlet parcels are the edge to check — Building By-law setbacks and flood construction levels follow from that dataset, parcel by parcel.

faq.a: It is not part of the West End, even though the City's areas page links the Coal Harbour locality name to the West End page.
faq.q: Is Coal Harbour a separate neighbourhood or part of Downtown?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals are separate: a strata can still restrict them and the City of Vancouver licences them. The Empty Homes Tax declaration applies if the unit sits empty instead.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Coal Harbour condo long-term?

faq.a: The residences are strata condominiums (Fairmont Pacific Rim Residences: Freehold Strata, Strata Plan BCS3699, 173 residences above a 377-room hotel; Paradox: 217 apartments alongside 147 hotel rooms), but the hotel components mean the Form B, air-space parcels and cost-sharing arrangements need reading, not just the suite documents.
faq.q: Is a unit in the Fairmont Pacific Rim or the Paradox a normal strata purchase?

faq.a: On the developer's own figures: Cascina (117 suites + 30 townhouses), Denia (86 suites + 4 townhomes) and Escala (98 suites + 7 townhouses), plus townhouse homes at 1 and 2 Harbour Green and 17 adjacent townhomes at Carina. The townhouse units are strata too, but they are documented separately in and are not apartment condos.
faq.q: Which Coal Harbour buildings have townhouses as well as apartments?

faq.a: Partly, by plan: the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan lists public street-end view corridors at Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero Streets to the water, and requires the waterfront walkway system to be continuous along the Coal Harbour waterfront. A specific unit's view is still a unit-by-unit check, not a plan guarantee.
None verified as standalone complexes; no named standalone townhouse complexes were found.
faq.q: Are there any real townhouse complexes in Coal Harbour?

faq.a: A strata lot in an apartment tower — MLS sub-type "Townhouse" describes the unit's two-level, ground-oriented layout, but built form governs: your strata is the tower, with its depreciation report, CRF and levy history. Read the tower's Form B package, not a townhouse-complex package.
faq.q: A listing calls a Coal Harbour unit a "townhouse." What am I actually buying?

faq.a: Under provincial law, strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, even where a listing still prints one. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw and are separately licensed by the City — and the Empty Homes Tax declaration is a separate annual filing every owner must make.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Coal Harbour townhouse-form unit long-term?

faq.a: A half duplex is one of two units in a two-unit building, split by a 2-lot strata plan or a fee-simple subdivision; a tower townhouse is neither.
faq.q: Are the townhouses at Cascina, Denia, Escala or the Harbour Green buildings half duplexes?

faq.a: No — R1-1 is the SSMUH framework where it applies, on Vancouver's house-lot districts.
faq.q: Does Vancouver's R1-1 multiplex framework apply to a Coal Harbour parcel?

faq.a: A Vancouver-only 3% tax with an annual property status declaration on every purchase — budget the declaration into closing, and the tax itself if the unit will sit empty.
faq.q: What is the Empty Homes Tax check?

faq.a: No — Downtown is the official local area, one of the City's 22 distinct areas, and Coal Harbour is a neighbourhood inside it with its own Official Development Plan; "Coal Harbour" is the Paragon sub-area name.
faq.q: Is Coal Harbour an official City of Vancouver local area?

faq.a: The Coal Harbour Official Development Plan (By-law 6754), covering the continuous waterfront walkway, public open space connections from the downtown core to the shoreline, and street-end views to the water and mountains at Burrard, Thurlow, Bute, Jervis, Broughton, Nicola and Cardero Streets.

Coal Harbour Community Centre, 480 Broughton Street, with multi-purpose rooms and a gymnasium, plus Harbour Green Park on the waterfront and Devonian Harbour Park, 1929 West Georgia Street, at the Stanley Park gateway.
faq.q: Which recreation facilities are in Coal Harbour?
